summary: Fumimasa Fukui (1934–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1978–2005).
Fumio Enomoto (b. 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1981–1986) and as a professor at Osaka University (~1997–2017).

Fumio Masutani (1902–1987) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1949–1953), Shizuoka University (~1953–1960), Taisho University (~1961–1977), and Tsuru University (~1977–1983).

Fumio Matsuda works in religious and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University and served as executive committee chairman for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions' 40th academic conference (attested 1997).

Fumio Ouchi (b. 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. After earning his doctorate at Otani University, he served there as assistant professor (~1992–1998) and professor (~1998–2018).
Fumio Shoji (b. 1979) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Rissho University (~1998–2007), where he later served as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (~2012).
Fumio Tamamuro (b. 1935) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Meiji University (~1954–1965) and later held an academic post there (~1967–2006).
Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1991) and held a post at Shimane Prefectural Junior College (attested 1997).

Futoshi Takehashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (attested 1992). He served as an assistant at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute of Teaching from 1995 to 1997.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (1866–1942) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev and Georg Bühler, he later held a post at Saint Petersburg State University (~1900–1942).
Félix Nève (1816–1893) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1838–1840) and Christian Lassen (~1840–1841) before becoming a professor at KU Leuven in 1841.
G. V. Aston is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Aston earned a PhD in philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under Paul Harrison.

G. V. Devasthali (1906–1994) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944) and held posts at H.P.T. Arts and R.Y.K. Science College (attested 1944) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

Gadjin Nagao (1907–2005) was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatai and Susumu Yamaguchi, he was Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University (1935–1971) and taught at Kyushu University (1956–1958).

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, committee member Frank E. Reynolds, and traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule (b. 1921) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a sub-editor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1954–1960) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied at the University of Washington (~1958–1964) in religious and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of California, San Diego (~1972–1980) and Princeton University (~1980–2000).

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit universities. He worked at Darbhanga Raj Library (1893–1902), Muir Central College (1902), and served as Allahabad University's Vice-Chancellor (attested 1937–1939).

Gangs zhun is a Tibetology scholar. They studied at Hainan College for Nationalities (until 1989) and completed a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under the supervision of Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under MA supervisor Hanna Havnevik and traditional teacher Lama Byambaa (attested 2008).
